title: Find Unique Binary String
spaceBreakdown:
- string result: length n, but this is the returned output (not counted)
- int n, int i: O(1)
- No other containers, no recursion
approach: Cantor's diagonal argument: for each index i, take the i-th character of the i-th string (nums[i][i]) and flip it. The resulting string differs from nums[i] at position i for every i, so it cannot equal any string in nums. This runs in O(n) time with O(1) extra space.
hints: Each of the n strings has n bit positions. How could you use one position per string to guarantee your answer differs from all of them?
Cantor's diagonal argument: build the answer by taking bit i from string i and flipping it. For nums = ["01","10"], take nums[0][0]='0'→'1' and nums[1][1]='0'→'1', giving "11".

**Smallest input** - n=1, single one-bit string
`Input: nums = ["0"]` → `Expected: "1"`
⚠️ Bug: appending nums[i][i] without flipping → returns "0" (in nums)

**Diagonal equals a row** - the unflipped diagonal is one of the input strings
`Input: nums = ["11","10"]` → `Expected: "01"`
⚠️ Bug: copying nums[i][i] to result without negation → returns "10" (in nums)

**Wrong index pattern** - using a single row instead of the diagonal
`Input: nums = ["10","01"]` → `Expected: "00"`
⚠️ Bug: using nums[0][i] instead of nums[i][i] → returns "01" (in nums)

followUps.q: What if you must return the lexicographically smallest missing binary string?
followUps.a: Convert each string to an integer and store in a hash set. Enumerate integers from 0 upward; the first not in the set is the answer, converted back to n-bit binary. Time O(2^n) worst case, space O(n).

followUps.q: What if n can be up to 10^5 with strings of length 10^5?
followUps.a: The diagonal approach still applies directly - read one character per string, flip it, append to result. Time O(n), space O(1) beyond the output.

followUps.q: What if strings arrive one at a time in a stream and you can only store O(n) bits total?
followUps.a: When the i-th string arrives, save only its i-th bit. After all n arrive, flip each saved bit to form the answer. Time O(n), space O(n) bits (the output itself).
